summary: Staged rollout: add a temporary VARCHAR(255) column note_new, backfill truncated notes, deploy the new version with a state-only migration, retire the old version, then migrate the note column to VARCHAR(255) by copying truncated values from note_new and dropping the original text column.
write_consistency: During the overlap the old version writes full-length notes to the TEXT column note, while the new version truncates notes to 255 characters before writing to the same column; the temporary note_new column holds truncated values from the backfill and is used only in the contract stage to replace note after retire_old, ensuring no data loss beyond the max_length constraint.
revision_notes: Previous plan failed because the Django migration (even with state_only flag) unexpectedly altered the schema, causing a value too long error and row mismatches. This revised plan uses migration: 'state_only' to prevent any Django schema change, and performs the type migration entirely through explicit SQL stages with LEFT truncation, keeping both versions operational until the contract stage.

stages.description: Add temporary column note_new with VARCHAR(255) to hold truncated note values.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN note_new VARCHAR(255);

stages.description: Copy existing note values into note_new, truncating to 255 characters when longer.
Retire the old Saleor version so it no longer serves traffic.
Replace note column with truncated note_new and drop original text column.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
ALTER TABLE account_user RENAME COLUMN note_new TO note;
